action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Call 'inspect' before a 'tap' on anything you have not located in this screen's tree, before answering what text a screen shows, and before reporting a control's state (a switch's value, whether a button is enabled, which tab is selected) or whether a sheet, alert or other modal is in front (the result says so) — never guess coordinates from memory of similar apps, and do not 'screenshot' for these. Go straight to 'screenshot' for color, images, and layout. Three reads: no marker and no x/y = the whole visible tree (the safe default when you do not know the exact label); marker = the first element, in tree order, whose label contains that CASE-SENSITIVE substring — a title can match before the button with the same text, so check the matched element's type; x/y = the element drawn on top at that point, as a tap would find it, with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container). If a marker misses or returns the wrong element, read the whole tree instead of guessing or screenshotting. Then tap the center of the target's frame. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted; text longer than its area shows is cut (it ends with ...). Only the x/y read resolves occlusion, and only by bars and containers it can recognize: a frame from the whole-tree or marker read that overlaps a later sibling (a tab bar, a sheet) may be covered, so before tapping it read x/y at its center; a point on a sheet's blank area can still read the content behind it, so when the result reports a modal, stay inside it. A tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with marker, or with x/y on the target itself: a point in a gap answers the container around it, which is no smaller; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the currently attached simulator, or the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

marker.description: For 'inspect': return only the first element (tree order, with its descendants) whose match_key attribute contains this case-sensitive substring — pass the label text exactly as the tree or the user wrote it, and prefer a distinctive fragment over a guess at capitalization. Omit for the whole tree (the safe default), or pass x/y instead for the element under a point.

match_key.description: For 'inspect' with 'marker': the attribute to match — label (default), value, or role (the element type, e.g. Button, Switch, TabBar — pass the exact name).

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_get_page
entries.description:
Get content of a specific Confluence page by its ID, or by its title and space key.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    page_id: Confluence page ID. If provided, 'title' and 'space_key' are ignored.
    title: The exact title of the page. Must be used with 'space_key'.
    space_key: The key of the space. Must be used with 'title'.
    include_metadata: Whether to include page metadata.
    convert_to_markdown: Convert content to markdown (true) or keep raw HTML (false).

Returns:
    JSON string representing the page content and/or metadata, or an error if not found or parameters are invalid.

page_id.description: Confluence page ID (numeric ID, can be found in the page URL). For example, in the URL 'https://example.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/TEAM/pages/123456789/Page+Title', the page ID is '123456789'. Provide this OR both 'title' and 'space_key'. If page_id is provided, title and space_key will be ignored.

title.description: The exact title of the Confluence page. Use this with 'space_key' if 'page_id' is not known.

space_key.description: The key of the Confluence space where the page resides (e.g., 'DEV', 'TEAM'). Required if using 'title'.

include_metadata.description: Whether to include page metadata such as creation date, last update, version, and labels.

convert_to_markdown.description: Whether to convert page to markdown (true) or keep it in raw HTML format (false). Raw HTML can reveal macros (like dates) not visible in markdown, but CAUTION: using HTML significantly increases token usage in AI responses.

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_search
entries.description:
Search Confluence content using simple terms or CQL.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    query: Search query - can be simple text or a CQL query string.
    limit: Maximum number of results (1-50).
    spaces_filter: Comma-separated list of space keys to filter by.

Returns:
    JSON string representing a list of simplified Confluence page objects.

query.description:
Search query - can be either a simple text (e.g. 'project documentation') or a CQL query string. Simple queries use 'siteSearch' by default, to mimic the WebUI search, with an automatic fallback to 'text' search if not supported. Examples of CQL:
- Basic search: 'type=page AND space=DEV'
- Personal space search: 'space="~username"' (note: personal space keys starting with ~ must be quoted)
- Search by title: 'title~"Meeting Notes"'
- Use siteSearch: 'siteSearch ~ "important concept"'
- Use text search: 'text ~ "important concept"'
- Recent content: 'created >= "2023-01-01"'
- Content with specific label: 'label=documentation'
- Recently modified content: 'lastModified > startOfMonth("-1M")'
- Content modified this year: 'creator = currentUser() AND lastModified > startOfYear()'
- Content you contributed to recently: 'contributor = currentUser() AND lastModified > startOfWeek()'
- Content watched by user: 'watcher = "user@domain.com" AND type = page'
- Exact phrase in content: 'text ~ "\"Urgent Review Required\"" AND label = "pending-approval"'
- Title wildcards: 'title ~ "Minutes*" AND (space = "HR" OR space = "Marketing")'
Note: Special identifiers need proper quoting in CQL: personal space keys (e.g., "~username"), reserved words, numeric IDs, and identifiers with special characters.

spaces_filter.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of space keys to filter results by. Overrides the environment variable CONFLUENCE_SPACES_FILTER if provided. Use empty string to disable filtering.

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_get_issue
entries.description:
Get details of a specific Jira issue including its Epic links and relationship information.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    issue_key: Jira issue key.
    fields: Comma-separated list of fields to return (e.g., 'summary,status,customfield_10010'), a single field as a string (e.g., 'duedate'), '*all' for all fields, or omitted for essentials.
    expand: Optional fields to expand.
    comment_limit: Maximum number of comments.
    properties: Issue properties to return.
    update_history: Whether to update issue view history.

Returns:
    JSON string representing the Jira issue object.

Raises:
    ValueError: If the Jira client is not configured or available.

fields.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of fields to return (e.g., 'summary,status,customfield_10010'). You may also provide a single field as a string (e.g., 'duedate'). Use '*all' for all fields (including custom fields), or omit for essential fields only.

expand.description: (Optional) Fields to expand. Examples: 'renderedFields' (for rendered content), 'transitions' (for available status transitions), 'changelog' (for history)

comment_limit.description: Maximum number of comments to include (0 or null for no comments)

properties.description: (Optional) A comma-separated list of issue properties to return

update_history.description: Whether to update the issue view history for the requesting user

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_search
entries.description:
Search Jira issues using JQL (Jira Query Language).

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    jql: JQL query string.
    fields: Comma-separated fields to return.
    limit: Maximum number of results.
    start_at: Starting index for pagination.
    projects_filter: Comma-separated list of project keys to filter by.
    expand: Optional fields to expand.
    page_token: Pagination token from a previous search result (Cloud only).

Returns:
    JSON string representing the search results including pagination info.

jql.description:
JQL query string (Jira Query Language). Examples:
- Find Epics: "issuetype = Epic AND project = PROJ"
- Find issues in Epic: "parent = PROJ-123"
- Find by status: "status = 'In Progress' AND project = PROJ"
- Find by assignee: "assignee = currentUser()"
- Find recently updated: "updated >= -7d AND project = PROJ"
- Find by label: "labels = frontend AND project = PROJ"
- Find by priority: "priority = High AND project = PROJ"

fields.description: (Optional) Comma-separated fields to return in the results. Use '*all' for all fields, or specify individual fields like 'summary,status,assignee,priority'

projects_filter.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of project keys to filter results by. Overrides the environment variable JIRA_PROJECTS_FILTER if provided.

page_token.description: (Optional) Pagination token from a previous search result. Cloud only — Server/DC uses start_at for pagination.

`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/ssr/contentSecurityPolicy.ts`, 275 lines. `useDefaults: true` (`:116`). `script-src` is at `:131-151` — an allowlist of third-party hosts only (Google Maps/Places, Adyen, Stripe, PayPal, Apple Pay, Measmerize, Klarna, `storage.googleapis.com`, `*.demandware.net`).

1. **Do not attach a nonce to the JSON-LD tag "to be safe."** Under CSP3, introducing any nonce or hash into `script-src` disables `'unsafe-inline'` for the whole directive. Adding a nonce to `script-src` risks the same class of regression against `'unsafe-eval'`/third-party payment scripts.
2. **React-helmet + JSON-LD content must go through `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`** or a single string child. Passing an object or interpolated fragments to a `<script>` child under helmet is a known source of silent empty output — budget a little time to verify the SSR'd bytes, not just the React tree.
3. **`script-src-attr` is `'none'`** (helmet default, not overridden) — irrelevant to JSON-LD, but means no inline event handlers if any vendor snippet is ever inlined.

Secondary issue: `ZimmermannUK` and `ZimmermannEUen` both resolve to locale `en-GB`, so any naive cross-linking would produce colliding `hreflang="en-gb"` entries.

**robots.txt: exists, allow-everything.** Served at `overrides/app/ssr.js:183` via `runtime.serveStaticFile('static/robots.txt')`, registered in the static glob at `config/default.js:225`. File is `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/static/robots.txt`, 23 bytes, in full:
```
User-agent: *
Disallow:
```
No disallow rules for `/checkout`, `/account`, `/search`, or filter params; no `Sitemap:` line. Note it is a single static file served identically to all 10 storefronts — per-storefront robots would need new routing.

**Sitemap: does not exist.** No generator, no route, no script. Every `sitemap` hit is either the footer column-width token (`overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts:13`) or a translation string. `worker/` and `scripts/` are clean.

## 4. SSR — confirmed, and Helmet output is injected server-side

`overrides/app/ssr.js` builds a full Express app via `runtime.createHandler` (`:125`) and terminates in `app.get('*', runtime.render)` (`:221`) — every storefront route is server-rendered. `overrides/app/ssr/` contains `connectionPools.ts`, `contentSecurityPolicy.ts`, `marketingCloud.ts`, `paymentMetadata.ts`, `slasTokens.ts`, `types.ts` — no SEO logic in any of them.

Helmet SSR injection, in `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-react-sdk/ssr/server/react-rendering.js`:
- `:387` — `const helmet = Helmet.renderStatic();`
- `:440` — `const helmetHeadTags = VALID_TAG_NAMES.map(tag => helmet[tag] && helmet[tag].toComponent()).filter(tag => tag);`
- `:442` — passed as `head: [...helmetHeadTags]` into `<Document>`, then `renderToString`'d.

**`script` is in the whitelist** — `:52`:
```js
const VALID_TAG_NAMES = ['base', 'body', 'head', 'html', 'link', 'meta', 'noscript', 'script', 'style', 'title'];
```

This is the answer you need for the JSON-LD ticket: a `<script type="application/ld+json">` declared inside `<Helmet>` **will** be serialised into the SSR'd `<head>`. The SDK's own test suite proves the pipeline end-to-end — `node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-react-sdk/ssr/server/react-rendering.test.js:229-232` renders exactly `type: "application/ld+json"` with `"@context": "http://schema.org"`, and `:649` asserts `head.querySelector('script[type="application/ld+json"]').innerHTML` contains it. No new SSR plumbing is required.

## 5. Structured data — definitively absent

Case-insensitive search for `ld+json|schema.org|itemProp|itemScope|itemType|microdata|JsonLd|StructuredData|structured-data`:

- **`overrides/`**: zero real hits. Every match is a TypeScript prop-type identifier whose name happens to end in `...ItemProps` (`ZimmIconAndTextItemProps`, `ZimmNavItemProps`, `ProductItemProps`, `selectCartItemProps`, etc.). No microdata attributes, no JSON-LD.
- **`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/`**: zero. Only `promo-code/index.jsx:103,114,161` and two checkout partials using an `itemProps` React prop passed to a Chakra `AccordionItem`.
- **`node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-react-sdk/`**: only the test file cited above.

**There is no structured data of any kind — no JSON-LD, no microdata, no RDFa — in the app or in the base template.** Product, CollectionPage, BreadcrumbList, ItemList, LocalBusiness, Organisation (PRD DMU-037 through DMU-041) are all greenfield. The PRD itself already records these as "custom build required, not OOTB in SFCC PWA Kit".

## 6. CSP — and the real answer on JSON-LD

`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/ssr/contentSecurityPolicy.ts`, 275 lines. `useDefaults: true` (`:116`). `script-src` is at `:131-151` — an allowlist of third-party hosts only (Google Maps/Places, Adyen, Stripe, PayPal, Apple Pay, Measmerize, Klarna, `storage.googleapis.com`, `*.demandware.net`).

Two things matter here:

**(a) There is no `'unsafe-inline'` and no nonce in `script-src`.** The nonce machinery in this file (`getOrCreateNonce`, `:96-112`) is **`style-src-elem` only** — built for SFCC-856 / Chakra-emotion and Contentful's un-nonceable injected `<style>` tags. `:183` is the only nonce consumer. `script-src` never receives a nonce or a hash.

Note also the two-layer merge: `overrides/app/ssr.js:129` applies `defaultPwaKitSecurityHeaders` **before** `helmet()` at `:131-135`. The runtime middleware patches `res.setHeader` and unions its required directives into whatever helmet emits (`node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-runtime/utils/middleware/security.js:40` — `'script-src': ["'self'", "'unsafe-eval'", runtimeAdmin, siteDotCom]`; union at `:107`). Final effective `script-src` ≈ the app allowlist ∪ `'self' 'unsafe-eval'` + MRT admin + site.com. Still no `'unsafe-inline'`, still no nonce.

**(b) This does not block JSON-LD.** `<script type="application/ld+json">` is a *data block*, not an executable script — the HTML spec's "prepare the script element" algorithm never classifies it as classic/module, so it is never executed and the CSP inline-script check is never invoked. Emitting JSON-LD requires **no CSP change**. I want to be precise rather than reassuring here, so three caveats for the estimate:

1. **Do not attach a nonce to the JSON-LD tag "to be safe."** Under CSP3, introducing any nonce or hash into `script-src` disables `'unsafe-inline'` for the whole directive. This file already documents that exact footgun biting them twice in `style-src-elem` (`:37-41` and `:200-209`, the latter noting a live 2026-09-07 breakage). Adding a nonce to `script-src` risks the same class of regression against `'unsafe-eval'`/third-party payment scripts.
2. **React-helmet + JSON-LD content must go through `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`** or a single string child. Passing an object or interpolated fragments to a `<script>` child under helmet is a known source of silent empty output — budget a little time to verify the SSR'd bytes, not just the React tree.
3. **`script-src-attr` is `'none'`** (helmet default, not overridden) — irrelevant to JSON-LD, but means no inline event handlers if any vendor snippet is ever inlined.

Other relevant CSP state: `'frame-ancestors': ["'self'", 'https://app.contentful.com']` (`:273`), `'style-src-attr': ["'unsafe-inline'"]` (`:218`), and `STRICT_CSP_PATH_PREFIXES` (`:48-61`) route-gating with site-alias stripping (`:84-88`) — note that list must stay in sync with `overrides/app/routes.tsx` if new SEO routes (e.g. a sitemap route) are added.

## 7. Multi-site config

**10 sites, each with exactly one locale.** `config/sites.js` (56 lines) merges two sources: `config/sites.generated.js` (SCAPI-derived, auto-generated by `npm run sync:regional-config`, last synced 2026-08-07) supplies locale/currency truth; `config/sites.overlay.js` (hand-maintained) supplies URL aliases and the `sfccSiteId` override. `sites.js:42` sets `defaultLocale: locales[0].id` — deliberately *not* SCAPI's site default, with the reasoning at `:35-41`.

From `config/sites.overlay.js:29-49`:

| PWA site id | SFCC site | Locale | URL prefix |
|---|---|---|---|
| ZimmermannAU | — | `en` | *(root, no prefix — default site)* |
| ZimmermannUS | — | `en-US` | `/us` |
| ZimmermannUSIntl | — | `en-CA` | `/en-ca` |
| ZimmermannUK | — | `en-GB` | `/uk` |
| ZimmermannEUen | ZimmermannEU | `en-GB` | `/en-eu` |
| ZimmermannEUfr | ZimmermannEU | `fr` | `/fr-eu` |
| ZimmermannEUit | ZimmermannEU | `it` | `/it-eu` |
| ZimmermannEUes | ZimmermannEU | `es` | `/es-eu` |
| ZimmermannEUIntl | — | `en-CH` | `/en-ch` |
| ZimmermannHK | — | `en-HK` | `/hk` |
| ZimmermannME | — | `en-AE` | `/en-ae` |

URL shape, `config/default.js:69-81`: `url.site: 'path'`, `url.locale: 'path'`, `showDefaults: false`, `showBasePath: false`. `defaultSite: 'ZimmermannAU'` (`:122`) with no alias, so AU lives at `/` and every other storefront carries a single leading alias segment (`:125-137`). Note the alias *is* the site ref — there is no separate locale segment, so paths are `/uk/product/x`, not `/uk/en-GB/product/x`.

`overrides/app/config/countries.ts` (128 lines) layers hand-maintained business data over `countries.generated.ts` (64 lines) — `shippingCountry`, `checkoutOwner` (`'sfcc' | 'global-e' | 'hybrid'`), `globalEPricing`, `boutiqueRegion`, keyed by URL slug. Its own header at `:9` lists **"hreflang generation"** as an intended consumer — but nothing in the codebase currently reads it for that purpose. It is the natural place to hang a cross-site hreflang map.

---

## Bottom line for estimating

**Exists today:** SSR on all routes (Helmet SSR-injected, `script` whitelisted); base `Seo` component (title/description/noindex/keywords, un-overridden); PDP/PLP title+description from SFCC `pageMetaTags`; a permissive static `robots.txt`; self-referential hreflang inherited verbatim from the base template; a well-documented CSP with per-request nonces on `style-src-elem` only.

**Does not exist at all:** canonical tags (any page), cross-site hreflang, XML sitemaps, OG/Twitter cards, structured data of any kind, per-storefront robots, and any `index, follow` affirmation. `DEFAULT_SITE_TITLE` is still `"Retail React App"`, the homepage still ships placeholder SEO copy, and the `/:segments+` catch-all — which serves the real PLP and content pages — emits no page-specific title or description on its success path.

**Three estimate-shaping gotchas:** (1) `supportedLocales.length === 1` per site means hreflang needs a brand-new cross-site resolver, not a tweak; (2) `og:` tags from Business Manager are currently rendered with `name=` instead of `property=` and are therefore inert; (3) JSON-LD needs no CSP change, but do not add a `script-src` nonce — this repo has already been burned twice by the CSP3 nonce-disables-unsafe-inline rule.</result>


Note line 379-381: the category from the **path** is injected into the refine array as `cgid=<id>` — i.e. the path segment is converted into a query-style refinement before hitting the API.

The actual parsing lives in `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-search-params.js`:

```js
// use-search-params.js:23-33
export const useSearchParams = (searchParams = DEFAULT_SEARCH_PARAMS, parseRefine = true) => {
    const {search} = useLocation()
    const searchParamsObject = { ...searchParams, ...parse(search.substring(1), parseRefine) }
    return [searchParamsObject, {stringify, parse}]
}
```
```js
// use-search-params.js:73-95
export const parse = (searchParamsStr, parseRefine = true) => {
    const params = queryString.parse(searchParamsStr, PARSE_OPTIONS)
    params.refine = Array.isArray(params.refine) ? params.refine : [params.refine].filter(Boolean)
    if (parseRefine) {
        params._refine = params.refine
        params.refine = params.refine.reduce((acc, curr) => ({
            ...acc,
            ...queryString.parse(curr, {...PARSE_OPTIONS, parseNumbers: false,
                arrayFormat: 'separator', arrayFormatSeparator: '|'})
        }), {})
    }
    return params
}
```

```js
export const useSearchParams = (searchParams = DEFAULT_SEARCH_PARAMS, parseRefine = true) => {
    const {search} = useLocation()
    const searchParamsObject = { ...searchParams, ...parse(search.substring(1), parseRefine) }
```

```js
// use-search-params.js:73-95
export const parse = (searchParamsStr, parseRefine = true) => {
    const params = queryString.parse(searchParamsStr, PARSE_OPTIONS)
    params.refine = Array.isArray(params.refine) ? params.refine : [params.refine].filter(Boolean)
    if (parseRefine) {
        params._refine = params.refine
        params.refine = params.refine.reduce((acc, curr) => ({
            ...acc,
            ...queryString.parse(curr, {...PARSE_OPTIONS, parseNumbers: false,
                arrayFormat: 'separator', arrayFormatSeparator: '|'})
        }), {})
    }
    return params
}
```

So the wire format is `?refine=c_refinementColor%3Dblack%7Cwhite&refine=c_size%3D8&sort=...&offset=...`. // use-search-params.js:73-95
```js
export const parse = (searchParamsStr, parseRefine = true) => {
    const params = queryString.parse(searchParamsStr, PARSE_OPTIONS)
    params.refine = Array.isArray(params.refine) ? params.refine : [params.refine].filter(Boolean)

    }
```

Base PLP navigates on **every** checkbox click (`toggleFilter` at `node_modules/.../product-list/index.jsx:328`). The Zimmermann override **buffers** all selections and commits in **one navigation on APPLY**.

**The buffering handler — index.tsx:567-589:**

```ts
const handleBufferedToggle = (
  value: { value: string | number },
  attributeId: string,
  selected: boolean,
  allowMultiple = true,
) => {
  const stringValue = String(value.value);
  if (!allowMultiple) {
    const current = pendingRefine[attributeId]?.[0];
    setValues(attributeId, current === stringValue ? [] : [stringValue]);
    return;
  }
  if (selected) {
    removeValue(attributeId, stringValue);
  } else {
    setValues(attributeId, [...(pendingRefine[attributeId] ?? []), stringValue]);
  }
};
```

## 1. Page Structure & Content

### 1.1 Layout (SPR-01, SPR-02 — Confirmed 2026-05-08)
- Dedicated category landing page; products displayed in a grid layout.
- "View more" pattern (not infinite scroll) loads additional products. The per-page count (currently 36) is handled in the FE — not configurable via BM (IC 2026-05-25).

### 1.2 Editorial / SEO Content (SPR-03, SPR-04 — Confirmed 2026-05-08)
- Editorial/SEO paragraph with a "read more" expand action (not collapsible — confirmed per 24.06 design review); positioned below YMAL / Recently Viewed (RJ note).
- Configurable title, description, and hero image per category page via Business Manager.
- Design TBC: hero image included in the page header; H1/description placement is exploring a discreet location or inline in page code.

### 1.3 Inline Editorial Hero (SPR-64 — Confirmed 2026-05-08)
- Optional editorial hero image rendered inline within the product grid (not in the page header).
- Optional headline and body text alongside the image; design may also include H1/H2 text elements.
- Configurable by business users in Business Manager.
- New feature introduced in Song UX redesigns.

### 1.4 Inline Category Links (SPR-65, SPR-66 — Confirmed 2026-05-08)
- Configurable set of inline category links displayed below the hero image and above the product grid.
- Links are contextual — an edit of subcategories (not all are shown).

# FED estimate audit — SFCC-173, SFCC-174, SFCC-724

## Cross-cutting finding (read this first)

**There are two parallel, unreconciled SEO backlogs in two different epics.**

| | Epic | Priority | Labels | Assignee | ACs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SFCC-173 / 174 / 724 | **SFCC-24 "Enhancements"** | Medium | `ENH-049`, `ENH-050`, `DMU-023` | 173/174 → Marcel; 724 unassigned | **none** |
| SFCC-557 … SFCC-578 (22 stories) | **SFCC-22 "SEO & Analytics"** | Low | `DMU-*`, `Squad-B` | all unassigned | real |

The SFCC-22 set already contains dedicated stories for the same work:

- **SFCC-562** — Canonical Tags on All Indexable Pages (`DMU-022`, `DMU-023`, `SPR-03`)
- **SFCC-563** — Canonical Tags on Filtered & Faceted PLP URLs — **carries label `DMU-023`, identical to SFCC-724**
- **SFCC-572** — Product & Merchant Listing Structured Data Schema (PDP) — **7 real ACs**
- **SFCC-573** — CollectionPage / BreadcrumbList / ItemList (PLP)
- **SFCC-566** — XML Sitemap · **SFCC-571** — robots.txt · **SFCC-577** — PLP SEO Copy Content Field (BM-configurable)
- **SFCC-576** — GEO Technical Foundations Readiness Check

Two of my three tickets are substantially duplicated there. Any sizing that doesn't reconcile the two epics double-counts.

**Baseline state — the whole SEO layer is greenfield.** Verified across `overrides/`, `config/`, `worker/` and `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/`:

- **Zero** `<link rel="canonical">` anywhere.
- **Zero** JSON-LD / microdata / RDFa anywhere.
- `overrides/app/static/robots.txt` is literally `User-agent: *` / `Disallow:` — blocks nothing.
- No sitemap generator, route or script.
- No `absoluteUrl()` helper.
- hreflang exists but is self-referential only — each site declares exactly one locale in `config/sites.overlay.js`, so `supportedLocales.length === 1` everywhere and the 11 storefronts never reference each other.
- Only SEO commit in history is `e8a874fc feat(plp): hierarchical category URLs` (DMU-014).

**Two corrections to the brief's premises:**

1. **It is 11 storefronts, each pinned to one locale** — not 8 sites × 11 locales. `config/sites.overlay.js:31-48`. Per-site SEO work multiplies by 11, but there is no site×locale matrix.
2. **The "3 days Testing" on SFCC-174 is not an estimate.** The Jira description records that cell verbatim as `Testing - what tool is doing this AI extraction?` — it is an unanswered question that got transcribed into a number column.

**One genuinely good piece of news:** JSON-LD needs no new SSR plumbing and no CSP change. `script` is in `VALID_TAG_NAMES` (`node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-react-sdk/ssr/server/react-rendering.js:52`) and Helmet output is serialised into the SSR'd `<head>` (`:387`, `:440`). `<script type="application/ld+json">` is a CSP data block, not an executable script. **Do not add a nonce to `script-src` "to be safe"** — under CSP3 that disables `'unsafe-inline'` for the whole directive, and `overrides/app/ssr/contentSecurityPolicy.ts:200-209` documents this repo being burned by exactly that on 2026-09-07.

---

## SFCC-173 — FAQ and Article Structured Data Schema via Contentful

**What it actually asks for:** author FAQ/Article content in Contentful and emit `FAQPage` / `Article` JSON-LD so care and editorial content can surface in AI Overviews.

**AC quality: NO — zero.** `customfield_10231` is null. The description is a pasted spreadsheet row with `Sizing: ?` and three blank Notes fields. Compare SFCC-572 in the same project, which has 7 testable ACs.

**What exists already**

| | Evidence |
|---|---|
| No FAQ content type | `scripts/contentful/content-types/` — 12 types, all nav/footer/UI-copy/size-guide. None editorial |
| No Article content type | same |
| No SEO/structuredData field on any content type | same |
| No FAQ page, route, or PRD | `overrides/app/routes.tsx` has no `/faq`, `/help`, `/article`, `/journal`; zero FAQ hits in `.docs/prd/` |
| No approved schema template | `.docs/vendor/sparroSchema.md` §6.2: *"FAQ / Article schema (DMU-042 GEO) — not in the Sparro deliverable; templates to be sourced from Google Search tools at implementation"* |
| **Contentful data is not available at SSR** | `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts:130,145` — `useEffect` + raw `fetch()`, not react-query. `withReactQuery` (`_app-config/index.tsx:320`) resolves SSR data via `react-ssr-prepass`, which only collects `useQuery`. Contentful-sourced JSON-LD would SSR **empty** |
| Reusable: `ZimmAccordion` | `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmAccordion/` (on this branch) — FAQ UI is largely free |
| Reusable: content-type pipeline | `npm run sync:contentful` + `install:contentful` — but **6 Contentful environments**, one install each, no batch flag |

**FED work breakdown**

| Item | Days |
|---|---|
| Model + install `faq`/`faqItem` (+`article`) content types across 6 Contentful envs | 1.0 |
| Make Contentful SSR-available — convert `useContentfulEntries` to react-query so `ssrPrepass` collects it. 6 runtime consumers to regression-check (`useUiCopy`, `useHeaderNav`, `useSizeGuide`, `footer`, `uiCopyProvider`, `zimmBenefits`) | 2.0 |
| JSON-LD emitter util + `FAQPage`/`Article` builders + Contentful RichText→plain-text + safe serialisation | 1.0 |
| Helmet wiring, per-storefront `@id` / `url` / `inLanguage` across 11 storefronts | 0.5 |
| Tests + story | 0.5 |
| Rich Results validation ×11 storefronts | 0.5 |
| *(if in scope)* build the FAQ/Article page — no route, no design, no PRD | +1.5–3.0 |

**Bottom-up FED total: 5.5 – 8.5 days**
- **5.5** assumes the FAQ/Article page already exists or is someone else's story, FAQ only (Article dropped), and the SSR gap is actually closed.
- **8.5** includes building the page itself.
- **3.0 (the table figure)** is only reachable by emitting the JSON-LD **client-side** — which fails DMU-030 (*"rendered server-side … without dependence on client-side JS"*) and therefore fails the ticket's entire purpose.

**Verdict vs table: UNSIZEABLE, and UNDER at every compliant reading. Delta +2.5 to +5.5 days.**
Biggest single reason: **Contentful data does not reach the server renderer today**, so the one thing the ticket exists to produce would be invisible to the crawlers it targets.

**Blockers / unknowns**

1. **Scope contradiction — DMU-035.** `.docs/prd/dataMigrationSeo.md:57`: *"SEO rules and attributes will live in **SFCC** per storefront (not Contentful)."* SFCC-173's premise is the exact opposite.
2. **Launch-scope contradiction — DMU-042.** `dataMigrationSeo.md:70`: *"No GEO-specific features are in launch scope."* SFCC-173 is labelled `MustHave`. And SFCC-576 already exists for GEO readiness.
3. No `FAQPage`/`Article` template is signed off by anyone.
4. No PRD describes the page the schema would attach to.
5. Localisation strategy undecided — field-level (the `footerConfig` pattern) vs key-encoded (the `sizeGuide` pattern, which explicitly forbids field-level).
6. The `regions` scoping field is itself still pending client sign-off (`.docs/integration/02-contentful.md` §10.1).

**Questions for a human**

- **Emma Kirwan / Miranda** — has SFCC-173 been deliberately pulled forward into launch scope, given DMU-042 says GEO is post-launch and SFCC-576 already owns GEO readiness?
- **Sparro / Tell No Lies** — who authors and signs off the `FAQPage`/`Article` templates? Nothing exists today.
- **Bianca Morley (reporter) / PO** — does this ticket include *building the FAQ/Article page*, or only adding schema to a page someone else builds? This is a 3-day swing on its own.
- **Integration lead** — is converting `useContentful` to react-query (6 consumers) acceptable in this story, or does it need its own ticket? It's the actual blocker.
- **PO** — DMU-035 says SEO attributes live in SFCC, not Contentful. Which wins?

---

## SFCC-174 — Structured Product Description Fields for AI Answer Extraction

**What it actually asks for:** genuinely unclear — either (a) emit product description data in JSON-LD, or (b) restructure the product description content itself into discrete fields.

**AC quality: NO — zero.** `customfield_10231` null. The ticket's own note is the scope question: *"Hardi to check if covered in JSON LD Template."*

**I can answer that note: yes, it is covered — by SFCC-572.**

**What exists already**

| | Evidence |
|---|---|
| **SFCC-572 already covers this** | "SEO — Product & Merchant Listing Structured Data Schema (PDP)", 7 real ACs, `ProductGroup` + `hasVariant` + per-variant `offers` + `description` |
| Sparro template already written | `.docs/vendor/sparroSchema.md` §3 — full `ProductGroup`/`Product` shape incl. `description`, `material`, `size`, `color`, `gtin` |
| **The discrete fields already exist in SFCC and are already fetched and rendered** | `c_fabricComposition` (= Sparro's `material`), `c_careInstructions`, `c_modelFit`, `c_sizeFit`, `c_stylingNotes`, `c_environmentalMessage`, `c_tabDescription`, `c_tabDetails`, `c_styleNumber` — rendered in `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/detailsAndCareContent.tsx`, `environmentalQualitiesContent.tsx`, `sizeGuideContent.tsx` |
| PDP already fetches everything needed | `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:273-300` — `variations`, `prices`, `images`, `availability`, `variationAttributes`, `variants`, plus `useProductInventory`. No new fetch |
| HTML→plain-text already solved | `richTextToPlainText` at `overrides/app/utils/richText.tsx:240` |

## SFCC-724 — Indexable Filter Pages with Per-Filter Metadata

**What it actually asks for:** let a merchandiser opt specific filter combinations (e.g. Dresses + White) into indexability with their own clean URL, title, meta description and SEO paragraph.

**AC quality: PARTIAL.** `customfield_10231` is null, but unlike the other two the description is a proper user story with context, a named dependency and an explicit "effort estimate required". ~4 implicit requirements (opt-in mechanism, clean URL, unique metadata, canonical override), none in testable form.

**The description's central premise is false in code.**

> *"Currently, all filtered PLP URLs canonicalise back to the base category page per DMU-023"*

There are **zero** canonical tags in the application. Verified by exhaustive grep across `overrides/`, `config/`, `worker/` and the base package. `robots.txt` blocks nothing. So today **every filter, sort and pagination permutation is already a fully crawlable, indexable 200 with duplicate title and description and no canonical**. This is not "override the canonical" work — there is no canonical to override. That baseline is SFCC-562 + SFCC-563, both To Do and unassigned.

**DMU numbering drift:** the ticket cites DMU-023, but the filtered-PLP-canonicalisation requirement is **DMU-022** (`.docs/prd/dataMigrationSeo.md:43`), already flagged Open with precisely this note: *"Zimmermann wants the ability to override the canonical on selected indexable filter pages."* DMU-023 is hreflang-on-canonical-PDP. There's a systematic +1 drift across the whole SFCC-557–578 label set (SFCC-571 robots.txt tagged `DMU-037` vs PRD `DMU-036`; SFCC-572 PDP Product tagged `DMU-038` vs PRD `DMU-037`). Worth one cleanup pass, not a per-ticket fix.
